title: Prioritization & orchestration rubric for hosted API enterprise requests (chat, streaming, toolchains, structured outputs)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Customer requests for hosted API features (chat streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs) arrive from multiple channels (support tickets, sales, CSM escalations, in-product feedback) with inconsistent detail and no unified prioritization. This causes long TTR, ad-hoc engineering effort, and missed enterprise SLAs.

Goal: Define an operational rubric and orchestration flow that standardizes intake, scores requests against enterprise signals (SLA risk, data sensitivity, cost/latency impact, implementation effort), and produces a deterministic action: accept for immediate scoped work, schedule into backlog with priority band and required artifacts, or reject with a clear rationale and suggested alternatives.

Scope: Hosted API feature requests only (chat streaming, tool/function-calling wiring, structured output formats). Excludes Dedicated/Private deployment-specific infra, billing changes, or pure documentation asks. Deliverables: 1) Scoring rubric spreadsheet and JSON-friendly schema for automation, 2) Triage playbook (roles/responsibilities), 3) Intake form template for CSM/Sales/Support, 4) Example triage outcomes and communication templates for enterprise customers.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Raman: Created ticket after synthesis session with Sales and Support. Initial problem statement and success criteria recorded. Asked for ENG and DX input for feasibility and UX constraints.

2025-02-12 - Devon Patel: Proposed initial priority signals: SLA exposure, customer ARR, implementation risk, security/data sensitivity, model/latency cost delta, compatibility with existing routes. Draft rubric started (link in links).

2025-02-13 - Sales feedback (internal): Field team favors explicit 'workaroundable' flag and quick-turn timelines < 4 weeks for pilot commitments. Requested signal for 'strategic customer' separate from ARR (e.g., partnership risk).

2025-02-14 - Engineering (ENG-18754 comment): Early feasibility check suggests streaming + tool-calling combined requests often require runtime scheduling changes — label as high engineering lift by default. Suggested adding 'compatibility delta' metric.
2025-02-15 - Design review: We need in-console intake copy and a compact scoring UI. Design to produce low-fi flows for triage dashboard (due 2025-02-20).
2025-02-17 - DevOps: Flagged that requests which require new model variants or quantization profiles should automatically trigger a Dedicated capacity review. Added as dependency.

2025-02-18 - PM sync: Decided to pilot rubric for two incoming enterprise requests this cycle. Action: finalize rubric and intake form by 2025-02-20, implement manual triage process, collect telemetry on time-to-decision and alignment with customer satisfaction.
